description: Attach a file from the user's computer to this tool's result so you can inspect it in your next step: a screenshot you took, a chart or page a script drew, a document, a log or a source file. Text comes back as text: up to 2,000 lines and 50 KiB, or else the start of the file and the bash command that reads the next part. Any other file is attached whole, as it is, with its media type, and the provider decides whether it can read it. If it can't, or the file is too large, the result says so: convert or cut it with bash (a smaller image, the pages you need, extracted text) and view that instead. Keep images you attach at most 2,000 px on their long edge; resize a copy with bash first. You may pass at most one of `pages`, `seconds` or `sheet` to ask a supporting model to read only that part of a document, audio/video file or spreadsheet. Models that don't support slices refuse locally without sending the file; when a sliced read is accepted, the whole file is still uploaded, stored and resent in the conversation until compaction. To keep the rest of a private or oversized file out of the request, cut out the part you need with bash and view that copy. Attached files stay in the conversation, so view only the files you need. A relative path is resolved against the working directory, and ~ is the user's home.

pages.description: Read only this 1-based page or closed page range of a PDF, document or slide deck, such as "5" or "14-16". The whole file is still sent and stored.

seconds.description: Read only this closed whole-second range of an audio or video file, such as "0-30" or "120-210" (end greater than start). The whole file is still sent and stored.

sheet.description: Read only this 1-based worksheet number of a spreadsheet, such as 2. The whole file is still sent and stored.

name: view_file
